meta.source: research round 2026-09-11 — Poland. Thomas: “read the handoff and then begin to Research Poland and add as many nodes and edges as you can.”
meta.note:
POLAND, FIRST ROUND OF ITS OWN. RESULT: 25 nodes, 30 dependencies, 1 relation, 5 dropped notes.

WHY THE STARTING POINT WAS NOT WHAT THE COVERAGE WORKBOOK SUGGESTED. HANDOFF 085 filed Poland under “narrow and complete” — 8 nodes, zero orphans, the EU-chain rounds having wired every node they minted. That reading held up: the Eurostat ESMS chain for Poland (HICP hi4, LFS employ_simslfs, national accounts na10 and nama_10_gdp) is genuinely finished, and a probe of 26 further Eurostat dataset codes under three national-metadata suffixes found NOTHING ELSE PUBLISHED for PL. So the yield was never going to come from Eurostat. It came from three places the corpus had not opened at all: NBP (no node before this round), the classification layer (PKD, KZiS, PKWiU, PKOB, KST — and, behind them, NACE Rev. 2 and ISCO-08, which the corpus did not have either despite 21 EU countries in the graph), and the statutory layer (four Polish Acts, plus the annual survey programme that Article 18 of the 1995 statistics law produces).

THE ROUTE, AND IT IS THE REUSABLE PART OF THIS ROUND. Every Polish host is 403 at the container's egress proxy and the bridge VM has no network at all, so the only way in was Thomas's Chrome. Chrome reads HTML fine but the extension is refused on the built-in PDF viewer (“Permission denied for reading page content on this domain”), and most of what matters here is PDF. What works: on a page of the publisher's own origin, a same-origin `fetch` of the PDF into a Blob plus a synthetic `<a download>` click puts the bytes in the user's Downloads folder, which `device_request_folder_access` then makes readable to `pdftotext` and `pypdf` on the bridge VM. THE TRAP: Chrome allows ONE automatic download per tab per origin and silently blocks the rest — no error reaches the tool, the JS reports 200 and the right byte count, and the file simply never lands. A fresh tab per PDF fixes it. Second trap: the download must be the LAST action in a browser_batch, because a `navigate` immediately after tears down the blob before the save commits. Six PDFs came across this way, the largest 23 MB.

THE OTHER READING LESSON, and it changed which quotes are gradeable: the Statistical Yearbook is bilingual in FACING COLUMNS, and `pdftotext -layout` interleaves Polish and English on every output line, so every English sentence looks shattered. `pypdf` reads it in column order and the English comes out whole. Both readings were taken; every span quoted from that volume was checked against the pypdf one. This is the “a PDF is read THREE ways and the best reading wins” rule meeting a layout rather than a line break.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. The COICOP citation in the yearbook's general notes names no edition and is dropped `no-document`, matching Thomas's 2026-09-08 ruling rather than re-opening it. The PKWiU upstream is dropped for the same class of reason — “international classifications and nomenclatures” names nothing. The Ministry of Finance layer is untouched because www.gov.pl is refused by the Chrome extension and unreachable everywhere else; that is a routing fact, not a corpus fact, and it is written up in `_dropped`. The Foreign Trade Statistics node is one verified title away and is the single highest-value thing left on the table.

reports.title: NACE Rev. 2 — Statistical Classification of Economic Activities in the European Community
title_aliases: Statistical Classification of Economic Activities in the European Community
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The EU's statutory industry classification, established by Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006 and derived from ISIC. Every EU member state's national activity classification is built on it; Poland's PKD 2007 is the first one wired here. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round — the corpus had ISIC, NAICS, ANZSIC and CPA but no NACE node at all, despite 21 EU countries in the graph.
reports.cadence_note: Revised about once a generation (Rev. 1 1990, Rev. 1.1 2002, Rev. 2 2006, Rev. 2.1 2023); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: International Standard Classification of Occupations (ISCO-08)
reports.description: The ILO's occupational classification, fourth iteration after ISCO-58, ISCO-68 and ISCO-88, published 2008. National occupational classifications are routinely built on it; Poland's KZiS is the first one wired here. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Revised roughly every twenty years; 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Classification of Types of Constructions (CC)
reports.publisher: Statistical Office of the European Communities (Eurostat)
reports.description: Eurostat's classification of building and civil-engineering works, issued 1997/1998 and adopted as the basis for several national construction classifications, Poland's PKOB among them. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round. Eurostat's RAMON page for it is gone; the URL is the Commission's own Interoperable Europe catalogue entry.
reports.cadence_note: Not revised since issue; 0.05 is the nominal once-a-generation rate the corpus uses for standards.

reports.title: OECD Benchmark Definition of Foreign Direct Investment 2008: Fourth Edition
title_aliases: OECD Benchmark Definition of Foreign Direct Investment
reports.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
reports.description: The OECD's standard for compiling foreign direct investment statistics, fourth edition, aligned with BPM6. Named by NBP as one of six international standards the Polish balance of payments is compiled to. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Four editions since 1983; 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: External Debt Statistics: Guide for Compilers and Users (2013)
reports.publisher: Inter-Agency Task Force on Finance Statistics / International Monetary Fund
reports.description: The TFFS external-debt compilation guide, 2013 edition, superseding the 2003 edition and updated for BPM6. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round off NBP's standards footnote, which cites it as “External Debt Statistics 2014” — a year the IMF's own page does not carry, which is why the Polish edge is B.
reports.cadence_note: Two editions, 2003 and 2013; 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: International Reserves and Foreign Currency Liquidity: Guidelines for a Data Template
reports.description: The IMF's reserves data template guidelines, the standard behind the SDDS reserves template. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round off NBP's standards footnote.
reports.cadence_note: Revised occasionally (2001, 2013); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Combined Nomenclature (CN)
reports.description: The EU's goods nomenclature for customs and external-trade statistics, built on the WCO's Harmonized System and reissued each year by a Commission Implementing Regulation under Council Regulation (EEC) No 2658/87. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round; Statistics Poland groups foreign-trade goods by it.
reports.cadence_note: A new annual version is published each autumn for the following calendar year.

reports.title: Regulation (EU) No 692/2011 of the European Parliament and of the Council concerning European statistics on tourism
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The EU instrument defining tourism statistics and the transmission programme for them. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round: the Statistical Yearbook's tourism chapter takes its definition of “tourism” from it by name.

reports.title: Directive 2009/42/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council on statistical returns in respect of carriage of goods and passengers by sea
reports.publisher: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
reports.description: The EU instrument governing maritime transport statistics. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round: the Statistical Yearbook says its seaport cargo, ship-traffic and passenger tables follow it.

reports.title: Ustawa z dnia 29 czerwca 1995 r. o statystyce publicznej
title_aliases: ustawy z dnia 29 czerwca 1995 r. o statystyce publicznej
reports.description: Poland's law on official statistics (Dz.U. 1995 nr 88 poz. 439, consolidated Dz.U. 2026 poz. 851). It constitutes the official statistics service, defines statistical confidentiality, and in Article 18 is the enabling provision for the annual Programme of Statistical Surveys of Official Statistics. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.

reports.title: Ustawa z dnia 29 sierpnia 1997 r. o Narodowym Banku Polskim
reports.description: The Act on Narodowy Bank Polski (Dz.U. 1997 nr 140 poz. 938, consolidated Dz.U. 2022 poz. 2025). Article 3 sets price stability as NBP's basic objective and adds financial-stability tasks; the Act also obliges NBP to compile the balance of payments and the international investment position and to report on them to Parliament and the Council of Ministers. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round. The English alias is the name NBP itself uses in its own English publications, which is where it was read.

reports.title: Ustawa z dnia 27 lipca 2002 r. Prawo dewizowe
reports.description: Poland's Foreign Exchange Act (Dz.U. 2002 nr 141 poz. 1178, consolidated Dz.U. 2022 poz. 309). Together with the Act on NBP it is the source of the reporting obligation that feeds the Polish balance of payments. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round; both aliases are read in NBP's own English methodological notes.

reports.title: Ustawa z dnia 23 grudnia 1994 r. o Najwyższej Izbie Kontroli
title_aliases: Act on the Supreme Audit Office
reports.description: The Act on the Supreme Audit Office (Dz.U. 1995 nr 13 poz. 59). Article 7(1)(1) obliges NIK to submit to the Sejm an analysis of the execution of the state budget and monetary policy guidelines. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round; the English alias is NIK's own title for its English translation of the Act.

reports.title: Polska Klasyfikacja Działalności 2007 (PKD 2007)
reports.description: Poland's activity classification, introduced on 1 January 2008 by the Regulation of the Council of Ministers of 24 December 2007 and derived from NACE Rev. 2. It is the grouping almost every GUS release is presented in. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Successive versions track the NACE revisions (PKD 2004, PKD 2007, PKD 2025); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Klasyfikacja Zawodów i Specjalności (KZiS)
reports.publisher: Minister Pracy i Polityki Społecznej / Główny Urząd Statystyczny (GUS)
reports.description: Poland's classification of occupations and specialisations, derived from ISCO-08 and introduced on 1 January 2015 by the Regulation of the Minister of Labour and Social Policy of 7 August 2014. Used to group councillors, paid employees and their earnings, and the unemployed. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round off the Statistical Yearbook's general notes.
reports.cadence_note: Reissued when ISCO is revised or the occupational structure changes; 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Polska Klasyfikacja Wyrobów i Usług 2015 (PKWiU 2015)
title_aliases: Polish Classification of Goods and Services
reports.description: Poland's product classification, introduced on 1 January 2016 by the Regulation of the Council of Ministers of 4 September 2015, replacing PKWiU 2008. The Statistical Yearbook says only that it was compiled on the basis of international classifications and nomenclatures without naming one, so no upstream edge is minted from that sentence. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Successive versions roughly every seven years (2004, 2008, 2015); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Polska Klasyfikacja Obiektów Budowlanych (PKOB)
title_aliases: Polish Classification of Types of Construction
reports.description: Poland's classification of construction works, introduced on 1 January 2000 by the Regulation of the Council of Ministers of 30 December 1999 and derived from Eurostat's Classification of Types of Constructions. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Not revised since introduction; 0.05 is the nominal once-a-generation rate the corpus uses for standards.

reports.title: Klasyfikacja Środków Trwałych 2016 (KŚT 2016)
reports.description: Poland's classification of fixed assets by type, introduced on 1 January 2017 by the Regulation of the Council of Ministers of 3 October 2016. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Reissued about once a decade (KST 2010, KST 2016); 0.05 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Rocznik Statystyczny Rzeczypospolitej Polskiej — Statistical Yearbook of the Republic of Poland
title_aliases: Statistical Yearbook of the Republic of Poland
reports.description: Poland's flagship annual statistical compendium, bilingual Polish/English, running to about 745 pages. Its general notes and per-chapter methodological notes are where GUS states which classifications, censuses and EU instruments the whole volume rests on, which is what made it the highest-yield single document of the 2026-09-11 Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Annual; the 2024 edition was published December 2024. (The 2024 PDF's embedded XMP title still reads “2023” — stale metadata, not a different volume: the cover, spine and title page all read 2024, checked character by character.)

reports.title: Narodowy Spis Powszechny Ludności i Mieszkań 2021
reports.description: Poland's 2021 population and housing census, reference date 31 March 2021, the benchmark every Polish population balance from 2020 onward is carried forward from. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Decennial (2002, 2011, 2021); 0.1 is that rate written as a number.

reports.title: Flash estimate of the consumer price index
reports.description: GUS's monthly advance estimate of the consumer price index, issued at the end of the reference month, about a fortnight ahead of the full CPI release. It is the number NBP's Monetary Policy Council has in hand when a Report closes. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly, published on the last working day of the reference month.

reports.title: Program badań statystycznych statystyki publicznej (PBSSP)
title_aliases: Programme of statistical surveys of public statistics
reports.description: The annual Programme of Statistical Surveys of Official Statistics, issued each year as a Regulation of the Council of Ministers under Article 18 of the 1995 law on official statistics. It enumerates every survey Polish official statistics will run in the year, its data sources and its respondents — which is why Eurostat's Polish national accounts metadata points at it for the detailed source list. Editions 2012 to 2027 are published on GUS's BIP. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: One programme per calendar year, adopted the preceding December and amended in-year by further regulations.

reports.title: Balance of payments
reports.description: Poland's balance-of-payments statistics, compiled by the central bank from direct reporting by resident entities supplemented by Statistics Poland's surveys and administrative data. NBP publishes a monthly balance of payments and a fuller quarterly one; this node is the monthly series. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round off NBP's own methodological notes.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly. NBP: “Monthly b.o.p. is published 44 working days following the end of a respective month.” A fuller quarterly balance of payments follows three months after the reference quarter.

reports.title: Inflation Report
reports.publisher: Narodowy Bank Polski (NBP) — Monetary Policy Council
reports.description: The Monetary Policy Council's assessment of macroeconomic developments influencing inflation, carrying the NECMOD-based projection of inflation and GDP prepared by NBP's Economic Analysis and Research Department. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Three times a year — March, July and November.

reports.title: Financial Stability Report
reports.publisher: Narodowy Bank Polski (NBP) — Financial Stability Department
reports.description: NBP's systemic-risk assessment of the Polish financial system, with stress tests and recommendations, published under the financial-stability task the Act on NBP gives the bank. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Twice a year — June and December.

reports.title: Monetary Policy Guidelines
reports.publisher: Narodowy Bank Polski (NBP) — Monetary Policy Council
reports.description: The monetary policy guidelines the Monetary Policy Council adopts each year and presents to the Sejm alongside the Council of Ministers' draft Budget, as Article 227(6) of the Constitution requires. They set the inflation target and the strategy for the year ahead, and their execution is what NIK audits alongside the state budget. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, adopted in September for the following calendar year.

reports.title: Analysis of the execution of the state budget and monetary policy guidelines
reports.publisher: Najwyższa Izba Kontroli (NIK) / Supreme Audit Office
reports.description: NIK's annual analysis of how the state budget and the monetary policy guidelines were executed, presented to the Sejm by the President of NIK and required of it by Article 7(1)(1) of the Act on the Supreme Audit Office. It is submitted together with NIK's opinion on discharging the Council of Ministers. Minted 2026-09-11 in the Poland round.
reports.cadence_note: Annual; presented to the Sejm in June for the preceding budget year.

_dropped.why: The Statistical Yearbook's General Note 7(4) names COICOP as one of the classifications it groups by — “the Classification of Individual Consumption by Purpose (COICOP), on the basis of which final consumption expenditure of products (goods and services) of the households sector as well as expenditure on consumer goods and services of households (also adopted for compiling price indices) are grouped” — and names NO EDITION. That is exactly the case Thomas closed on 2026-09-08 when he dropped iq-cpi, tn-ins-cpi and ma-hcp-ipc -> un-coicop-2018 for the same reason, and PLAYBOOK 7d records it as a decided call. Recorded here rather than wired so the next Poland round does not re-derive it: the citation is real, the edition is not stated, and the corpus models COICOP editions as separate nodes.

PKWiU 2015 is the one Polish classification in the Statistical Yearbook's General Notes whose derivation is stated without a target: “PKWiU 2015, compiled on the basis of international classifications and nomenclatures, was introduced on 1 January 2016”. PKWiU is in fact built on the EU's CPA, which IS in the corpus as `cpa` — but the yearbook does not say so, and knowing it is not evidence. A round with the PKWiU introducing regulation (Dz.U. 2015 poz. 1676) in hand should close this; its enacting formula and explanatory notes are the place the CPA link would be stated.

NBP's methodological notes name the largest single input to the Polish current account by a title that is NBP's, not GUS's: “The main source of data on goods in the Polish balance of payments is Foreign Trade Statistics (FTS) compiled by the Statistics Poland on the basis of INTRASTAT declarations (for intra-European Union trade) as well as from the Single Administrative Documents, SAD (for extra EU trade)”. The sentence is first-party, exact and would carry an A — what is missing is the node, and minting one titled “Foreign Trade Statistics” would break the rule that a node carries the PUBLISHER's own title for the artefact. GUS's English foreign-trade pages redirected to its new portal (new.stat.gov.pl) mid-session and the release's own title was not read, so the node was not minted. One page away: find GUS's own title for the release, mint it, and this edge plus the INTRASTAT and SAD chain behind it all follow.

_dropped.why: ROUTING FINDING, worth recording because it shaped what this round could do. Of the Polish hosts, nbp.pl, stat.gov.pl, bip.stat.gov.pl, www.nik.gov.pl, isap.sejm.gov.pl and ec.europa.eu were all reachable in Thomas's Chrome; www.gov.pl and finanse-arch.mf.gov.pl were refused by the extension with “Navigation to this domain is not allowed”. Neither the cloud container nor the bridge VM has egress to any Polish host at all — the container's proxy answers 403 to CONNECT for every one of them and the bridge VM has no network. So the whole Ministry of Finance layer is unresearched rather than absent: the Public Finance Sector Debt Management Strategy, the state budget execution report NIK audits, and the Medium-Term Fiscal-Structural Plan are all on www.gov.pl. A future round needs either a gov.pl permission in the Chrome extension or a different network.

The Inflation Report's Figure 2.15 is titled “Number of people employed according to the LFS” and its source line reads “Source: Statistics Poland (GUS) data.” — so the figure names the artefact only by a three-letter acronym and the source line names only the agency. Neither half reaches the naming bar on its own, and PLAYBOOK 7a's chart-caption rule turns on the SOURCE LINE, which here is agency-only.
